messages:
Ivy: Noticed a spike in etcd round-trips and apiserver 500s in ap-south1 during a GPU onboarding batch. NVMe iowait and compactor jobs overlap with attach churn.

Ravi: seeing it too. etcd leader CPU ~95% and disk util 99%, follower lag climbing. apiserver errors look like EOFs when talking to etcd.

infra-bot: alert: etcd_disk_iops_utilization > 90% (ap-south1-main)

Noah: timeline: 12:02 bulk-provision job started (500 nodes), 12:05 etcd compactor kicked (scheduled cron at 12:05), 12:06 apiserver p50->p95 jump and controller-manager reconcile backlog grows.

Jen (oncall): oh no. compactor + mass attach = bad. We should avoid compaction during heavy control-plane write windows. Short term: pause compactor cron and lower provisioner concurrency.

Marco: agree. Also we should tune etcd's autosnapshot and compaction window; the compactor is single-threaded and causes bursty disk writes. If we can't avoid compaction we can pre-warm disk throughput or move compactor to a separate NVMe pool.

Ivy: example etcd log snippet:
```
2026-03-21 12:06:07.123456 W | rafthttp: got unexpected EOF from 10.0.5.7:2380
2026-03-21 12:06:07.223456 E | mvcc: store.command: apply t=0.000s err="mvcc: store is too slow"
```

Ravi: mitigation plan: 1) pause compactor cron (cronjob/etcd-compactor) 2) set provisioner MAX_ATTACH=8 3) cordon the onboarding batch (scale down parallelism) 4) scale etcd disk iops temporarily (request increase from cloud)

Noah: I'm going to run the cordon and patch the cron now.

Noah: commands:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch cronjob/etcd-compactor -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/provisioner PROVISIONER_MAX_ATTACH=8
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/bulk-onboard --replicas=2
```

infra-bot: action: patched cronjob/etcd-compactor (suspend=true) by Noah

infra-bot: metric update: etcd_disk_iops_utilization -> 64% (down from 98%)

Jen (oncall): apiserver 500s fell back to baseline, follower lag clearing. Good immediate relief.

Marco: cost note: temporarily bumping disk IOPS will add ~1.8k USD/day for this region if we keep it for 24h. For short mitigation it's fine but we need a longer-term plan.

Ivy: long-term proposals: (a) stagger compactor across followers, (b) add compaction-safety window tied to onboarding schedule, (c) provision a dedicated NVMe pool for etcd (higher cost but predictable), (d) add an admission check in bulk-onboard to query etcd util before starting.

Ravi: +1 for admission check and compactor window. Also we should add auto-throttle: if etcd_iops_util>80% or follower_lag>5s, reduce provisioner parallelism automatically.

Noah: I'll open a follow-up issue with a runtime flag to query etcd stats before bulk job start and a webhook to abort if unsafe.

Ivy: TODOs: Noah -> revert compactor suspend after window review (or reschedule), Marco -> cost calc for dedicated NVMe and ops runbook, Ravi -> implement auto-throttle proposal, Jen -> monitor for 1h and escalate if leader re-elections resume.

Jen (oncall): keeping watch. ping if you need me to re-open the compactor for testing. :eyes:
